a1-adv-kurz: Your boss asks you to explain the plan in just a few words, not a long speech.
You tell a neighbour at the door that you will talk to her for only a minute, because you are in a hurry.
The phone rings during dinner. You say you will be back in a moment. Which adverb means 'for a short time' or 'in a few words'?
a1-v-verstehen: The teacher explains the grammar twice and now you finally get the meaning. You say: ah, I see what it means now.
A tourist speaks very fast on the phone and you cannot follow what she says. You do not grasp it at all.
Your friend tells a joke in another language. You laugh because you got the point.
a1-n-pommes-frites: At the fast food counter you order a paper bag of long golden potato sticks with ketchup.
Children at the pool bar ask for hot, salty sticks of fried potato to eat with their burger.
The waiter asks what side dish you want with your sausage, potato salad or the fried potato sticks.
a1-n-information: At the train station you ask the clerk for facts about the departure time of the next train.
You read a website to learn facts about the opening times of the museum.
A leaflet gives you all the details you need about the hotel. What do you call these facts and details?
a1-n-foto: On holiday you hold up your phone and click to capture your family in front of the beach.
Your grandmother has an old black-and-white image of herself as a girl, in a frame on the wall.
You send your friend the image from the party. What do you call this picture taken by a camera?
a1-v-lieben: You say to your wife that she is the most important person in your life and that you have deep feelings for her.
A mother tells her baby, with a gentle voice, that she has very strong feelings of affection for him.
In a song the singer says that he has deep feelings for a girl. Which verb is this, stronger than 'to like'?
a1-pr-jeder: The teacher says that all students, one by one, will get a book. She means each single person.
At the party, one by one, each guest gets a little gift.
The sign says that any person who enters must wear a helmet. Which word means each, one at a time?
a1-n-taxi: It is midnight, there is no bus any more, so you phone for a car with a driver and a light on the roof to take you home.
At the airport you stand in the queue outside to ride in a yellow car and pay by the kilometre.
Your friend is drunk, so you call for a car with a meter that will take him to his flat.
a1-adj-lustig: Your friend tells a story about his cat and everybody laughs out loud for ten minutes.
At the party the guests are in a good mood and enjoy themselves, laughing and dancing.
A film about two clowns makes children laugh a lot. Which adjective describes the film?
a1-n-lehrer: At school a man stands in front of the class and explains maths to the pupils.
A man in your language course corrects your homework with a red pen and gives you marks.
Your son says that the man who teaches him German is very strict. Who is he?
a1-v-koennen: You tell the teacher that you know how to swim and are able to do it for 500 metres.
A friend asks if you are capable of speaking German. You say yes, a little.
The boss asks whether it is possible for you to come early tomorrow. Which verb expresses ability or possibility?
a1-n-gramm: The recipe says to add 250 of these of flour. It is a thousandth of a kilo.
At the post office the letter weighs only twenty of these.
At the market the seller weighs a hundred of cheese on the scale. Which small unit of weight is it?
a1-adv-hier: You hand something to your friend and say: it is in this place where I am standing, right at this spot.
At the school the teacher takes attendance. A pupil raises his hand and says: I am present in this place.
A tourist asks where the museum is, and you point to the ground and say it is in this very spot. Which adverb means 'in this place'?
a1-n-anrufbeantworter: You call your friend but nobody picks up. A machine records your voice and plays it later.
When you come home, the phone shows a red light because someone left you a message while you were out.
Your mother does not answer her phone, so you leave a spoken message on the device that records calls.
a1-n-hunger: It is two o'clock and you have not eaten since breakfast. Your stomach is growling and you need food.
After a long hike the children shout that they could eat a whole pizza, because they feel the need to eat.
A refugee has not eaten for two days. What strong feeling does he have?
a1-v-schliessen: It is cold and the wind comes in, so you go to the window and push it shut.
At six in the evening the shopkeeper turns the key and the shop is no longer open.
The teacher asks you to shut the door, so the noise from the corridor doesn't disturb the class.
a1-n-automat: You put coins into a big box at the station and get a bar of chocolate and a cold drink.
At the bank you put in your card and get cash out from the wall.
You need a ticket for the bus, but there is no clerk, only a box with a screen where you pay with coins.
a1-adj-automatisch: When you walk up to the shop, the doors open on their own, with no person pushing them.
Your coffee machine switches itself off after twenty minutes without you touching it.
The car has a gearbox that changes gears by itself. Which adjective describes this?
a1-n-nachmittag: Between lunch and dinner, around three o'clock, you drink coffee and the children come back from school.
The doctor's office is closed in the morning but open from 2 to 6 pm. Which part of the day is it?
You say: I am free from midday until the evening. Which part of the day comes after noon?
a1-n-dreiviertelstunde: The lesson at the language school is shorter than a normal hour. It lasts exactly 45 minutes.
The doctor says the treatment takes three quarters of one hour, not a whole hour.
The bus ride into town takes 45 minutes. Which single word means three quarters of an hour?
a1-v-sich-freuen: Your friend phones to say she is coming to visit next week. You feel very glad about it.
The children shout with joy because it is snowing outside and they can go sledging.
You get the news that you passed the exam and your face lights up. Which verb describes this feeling of being glad?
a1-n-ausgang: At the cinema you follow the green sign with a running man on it to leave the building.
The teacher says that when the fire alarm rings, you should leave through the way out marked on the plan.
At the supermarket you pay at the till, then walk through the door that leads outside. What is it called?
a1-n-jahr: It has twelve months, from January to December, and then a new one starts at midnight on New Year's Eve.
You say that your sister is 25 of these old. What unit of time?
You have lived in Germany for three of these, from 2021 until now. Which unit?
a1-adv-einfach: The teacher says the exercise is not difficult at all, you can do it without any trouble.
You are asked why you did not come to the party. You answer that you did not feel like it, nothing more, for no special reason.
The instruction says: just press the green button. Which adverb means 'simply' or 'just'?
a1-n-quadratmeter: The estate agent says that the flat has 60 of these. It is a unit of area, written m².
You buy a carpet for the living room and the shop asks how much area you need in these units.
A farmer says the garden measures a hundred of these. Which unit of area is that?
a1-v-waschen: Your hands are dirty after the garden work, so you use soap and water to clean them.
There is a pile of dirty T-shirts and socks, so you put them in the machine with powder.
Before dinner a mother tells her child to clean his hands. Which verb describes cleaning with water?
a1-pr-dich: You look at your friend and say that you can see him well. The word shows that he is the object of 'I see'.
A mother says to her son: I love you. Which word means 'you' as the object, for a person you say 'du' to?
You ask a friend: Can I call you tomorrow? Which pronoun means 'you' as the object or 'yourself' with a reflexive verb?
a1-adj-arbeitslos: After the factory closed, Mr Braun has no job and gets money from the state while he looks for work.
At the job centre many people queue because they do not have work at the moment.
A friend says he lost his job last month and still has not found a new one. Which adjective describes him?
a1-n-kollege: A man who works in the same office as you helps you with a computer problem.
You say about the man at the next desk that he is the person you work with every day.
On Friday you go for a drink after work with the man who works in your team. Who is he?
a1-n-sohn: A mother shows a photo of a little boy in a football shirt, her male child.
A father is proud: his male child has just passed his driving test.
On the form you write the names of your children. Under the male child you write: ...
a1-v-schreiben: You take a pen and put your thoughts on paper, one word after another, for a birthday card.
Your teacher asks you to put the answers into your notebook in good handwriting.
You type a long email to your friend on the computer. Which verb describes what you do with words?
a1-n-morgen: The sun comes up, birds sing and you drink your first coffee before going to work.
At 7 o'clock in the early part of the day you take a shower and have breakfast.
A friend asks which part of the day comes between night and noon. Which noun?
a1-n-gepaeck: At the airport you put two big suitcases and a bag on the belt to be checked in.
The train is full and there is no room on the rack for the cases and bags that you carry.
The hotel porter carries all your bags to the room. What is the word for all of your bags and suitcases together?
a1-n-familienstand: A form asks: single, married or divorced? This is the box you fill in about your relationship situation.
At the town hall the clerk asks about your situation in terms of marriage. What do you call it?
On the visa form there is a line asking if you are married or not. What is the name of the line?
a1-adj-meist: You say that the greatest number of your friends live in the city, nearly all of them. Which adjective?
The teacher says that the largest part of the class passed the exam. Which word means the greatest part?
The sentence says: the largest amount of people take the bus to work. Which word means 'the greater majority'?
a1-v-stehen: The bus is full, so you do not sit but remain on your feet near the door.
Where is the book? It is on the shelf, upright, next to the lamp.
The tourist asks where the cathedral is, and you say it is in the middle of the town square.
a1-adv-auch: Your friend says he likes pizza. You say that you like pizza as well. Which little word means 'as well'?
A teacher says that one student came late and another student was late too. Which adverb means 'too'?
You say 'I am hungry' and your sister adds: me too. Which word means 'too'?
a1-n-zigarette: A man stands outside the office, lights a small white paper tube filled with tobacco and blows smoke.
A doctor tells you to stop smoking small tobacco sticks because they are bad for your lungs.
At the kiosk a man buys a pack of twenty small paper tubes with tobacco.
a1-n-erwachsene: The sign at the cinema says that children under twelve pay half price, but grown people pay full price. Who pays full price?
A teacher says that when a child turns eighteen, he becomes a person who is no longer a child.
The sign at the swimming pool says that this pool is only for people over eighteen years old, not for children.
a1-n-land: You live in Germany. A friend asks which one you come from, Italy or France.
You leave the city for a weekend on a farm, with fields and cows, far from the traffic.
On the map you see borders. Each area with its own government and flag is called what?
a1-v-bleiben: It is raining heavily, so you decide not to go out and stay at home all day.
The teacher says to the children: do not get up, remain in your places.
You say to a friend: I will not leave the hotel until Friday; I keep my room until then.
a1-n-mai: It is the month in spring after April and before June. It is the fifth month.
On the first of this month people have a day off for Labour Day.
The flowers are blooming and the weather is getting warm. Your birthday is in the month between April and June.
a1-n-datum: On the invitation card you write the day, the month and the year of the party, such as 12 March 2025.
The clerk asks you to write today's day, month and year at the top of the form.
On the milk bottle there is a printed day after which you should not drink it. What do you call this information?
a1-adj-bekannt: Everybody in the country has heard of this singer; he has been on TV many times.
You say that the street looks like something you have seen before, you have been here already.
The Eiffel Tower is a landmark that people all over the world recognise. Which adjective describes it?
a1-v-moegen: A waiter asks if you enjoy fish. You say that you do and that it is one of your favourite dishes.
You say that you have a liking for your new colleague because she is friendly.
A child says to his mother that he is fond of chocolate. Which modal verb means 'to like'?
a1-n-bein: After running a long marathon, the part of your body between your hip and your foot hurts a lot.
The doctor puts a plaster cast on the injured limb of the footballer, between hip and foot.
A child sits on a chair and cannot touch the floor because the limbs that go down to the feet are too short.
a1-pr-dies: You hold up a book in a shop and ask: how much does this one here cost? Which word means 'this'?
The teacher points to three pictures on the wall and asks you what these are. Which word means 'these'?
Your friend asks which one of the two jackets you want. You point to the one near you and say: that one. Which word?
a1-n-schuelerin: A girl of twelve with a school bag goes to class every morning.
A teacher says that a young female pupil in the second row asked a good question.
On the school trip the teacher counts the children and says that one girl in her class is missing.
a1-adv-wann: You want to know the time of the party and ask: at what time does it start? Which question word?
A friend says he will come to visit you. You ask on which day or at which time.
The teacher asks the class: at what moment in history did the war end? Which question word means 'at what time'?
a1-n-buch: You sit in the evening with a lamp and read a long story with many pages and a cover.
At the library you take out a thick volume about history with a hard cover.
A friend gives you a novel for your birthday. What is it called?
a1-v-leben: You have lived in a small town since you were born. Which verb means to be alive and to have your home there?
The doctor says your grandfather is old, but he is still alive and breathing well. Which verb means 'to be alive'?
A friend asks where you currently reside, and you say: in Berlin, in a small flat. Which verb fits?
a1-n-bad: You fill the tub with warm water and foam and relax in it after a long day.
The flat has a kitchen, two bedrooms and a room with a toilet and a shower.
On holiday you go to a place where you can enjoy warm pools, massages and saunas.
a1-adj-geboren: On the form you write the place and the year when you came into the world: for example, 1990 in Dhaka.
A mother says that her baby arrived in the world last night. The baby is newly ...
The passport says that the holder came into this world on 5 May 1985. Which adjective goes before the date and place?
a1-n-einladung: You receive a card in the post asking you to come to your friend's wedding next month.
Your colleague sends you an email with the time and the place of her birthday party and asks you to join.
Your neighbour gives you a note asking you to come for dinner on Saturday. Which word means this kind of request to come?
a1-n-fisch: At the market you buy a salmon and put it in the fridge to cook it for dinner.
In the pond in the park you see an orange animal with fins swimming under the water.
The restaurant offers the choice between meat and a dish from the sea or river, such as trout. Which food?
a1-v-warten: The bus is late and you stand at the stop for twenty minutes, looking at the street.
You sit in the doctor's office and have to be patient until the nurse calls your name.
The mechanic says he must check the car regularly, so you bring it in every year for inspection.
a1-n-beispiel: The teacher says: if you do not understand the rule, here is a sentence that shows how it is used.
You tell your friend that many fruits are healthy, such as apples. What is the word for something that illustrates a general point?
In the book, next to each rule there is a sample sentence. What do we call such a sample?
a1-n-freund: A man you like a lot, you share secrets and go to football together with him. He is not your relative.
A girl says to her mother that the man she is dating will come for dinner tonight.
You introduce a man from your football team: he is a very good male companion of mine.
a1-adv-also: The teacher says: it is already late, so let us stop. Which small word means 'therefore' or 'so'?
A friend says: I have no money, so I cannot come. Which small word introduces a result?
The teacher sums up: we have read the text, therefore you can now do the exercise. Which small word means 'therefore'?
a1-v-aussehen: You see a friend who has not slept; you say he seems tired and pale.
The cake in the shop window looks delicious. Which verb means 'to give the impression' by appearance?
A mother says: you appear very happy today. Which verb describes this impression?
a1-n-formular: At the town office the clerk gives you a paper with boxes where you write your name and address.
You have to register your new flat, so you fill in a sheet with empty lines and tick boxes.
The doctor asks you to write your medical history on a printed sheet at the reception.
a1-adj-langsam: The old man crosses the street with his stick, one small step at a time.
The teacher asks the foreign student to speak at a low speed so that everybody can follow.
The snail needs ten minutes to cross the path. Which adjective describes it?
a1-n-cent: A pack of chewing gum costs one euro and fifty of these. Which small coin is a hundredth of a euro?
You get ten of these as change from the baker, a very small coin.
The bill says 4,99 euros. The last part, 99, is how many of this small unit?
a1-n-samstag: The day after Friday is when you do not work, and you go shopping and meet friends.
The weekend begins on this day, the day before Sunday.
Football matches in the league are usually played on this day of the week. Which day is it?
a1-v-legen: You take the newspaper and put it flat on the table, not upright.
The mother puts the baby in the bed on his back, in a flat position.
The waiter puts the knife and the fork flat next to the plate. Which verb describes placing something horizontally?
a1-pr-ihn: You see your brother in the street and wave to him. Which pronoun means 'him' as the object?
You ask about the dog: have you seen it? Which pronoun, for a masculine noun, replaces 'the dog'?
A colleague asks about the new boss. You say: I saw him yesterday. Which word means 'him'?
a1-n-gemuese: At the market you buy carrots, tomatoes and onions. Mothers say children should eat more of these.
The doctor says that you should eat five portions of plants like carrots, spinach and cabbage every day.
A vegetarian friend says he eats lots of broccoli and cucumbers but no meat. What food is it?
a1-n-sekunde: The athlete runs 100 metres in just ten of these, the smallest unit on the watch.
A minute has sixty of these. Which unit of time?
The traffic light changes in only a few of these, a very tiny part of time.
a1-n-platz: The bus is full and there is no free chair for you, so you stand. Which word means a spot to sit?
In the middle of the city there is a big open area with a fountain and cafés, where people meet.
You look for a spot to park your car, but the car park is full. Which noun?
a1-v-vorstellen: At a party you tell your friend: let me tell you who this is, this is my colleague, Tom.
Close your eyes and form a picture in your head of a beach with palm trees.
At the job interview you tell the manager about yourself: name, age and your experience.
a1-adj-bester: Anna's grade is the highest in the class. She is the top pupil among all.
At the restaurant the waiter says that the fish is the finest on the menu. Which adjective?
You win the race and everybody says you are the greatest, number one. Which adjective (superlative of 'good')?
a1-n-salat: A mix of green leaves with tomato and cucumber in a bowl with oil and vinegar as a starter.
At the supermarket you buy a green round head of leaves for your sandwich.
The waiter asks if you want chips or a plate of cold, mixed vegetables as a side dish.
a1-adv-leider: You want to come to the party, but you have to work. You say with regret that you cannot come. Which adverb expresses regret?
The shop assistant says with sadness that the jacket in your size is sold out. Which adverb starts her sentence?
The doctor says, sadly, that he has no time today. Which adverb means 'what a pity' at the start of a sentence?
a1-n-treppe: The lift is broken, so you walk up to the third floor on the steps.
In the old house, a wooden construction with many steps connects the ground floor and the first floor.
A child falls down the steps in the school building and hurts his knee.
a1-v-sehen: You open your eyes in the morning and notice the sun through the window, and a bird on the tree.
On Saturday you and your friends look at a football match on the TV.
The doctor asks if you can make out the letters on the wall. Which verb is it?
a1-n-bahn: You do not drive to work. You travel on rails and a fast vehicle takes you to the next city.
On the sports field there are lines for runners. Each runner stays within one of these lanes.
The railway company announces that a service to Hamburg has been delayed by ten minutes.
a1-n-eltern: On a family photo you see a girl and the two grown people who raised her, her mother and father.
The teacher says she wants to talk to the mother and father of the pupil at the meeting.
A child says that his mother and father will pick him up from school. Which plural noun means both?
a1-n-familie: On Sunday the mother, father, children and grandparents sit together at the table for lunch.
You say that you have a mother, a father, two brothers and a sister who live in the same house.
On the form: how many persons are in the household related to you? Which word means this group?
a1-adj-naechste: The bus has just left. The driver says that the one that comes after this one arrives in ten minutes.
The teacher says: let us meet again in the week that follows this one.
At the supermarket the cashier calls out to the person who is directly after the customer she is serving. Which adjective means 'the one that follows'?
a1-v-bitten: You politely tell the waiter that you want him to bring you a glass of water. You request it kindly.
The old lady asks you, with a friendly voice, to carry her bag up the stairs.
Your boss asks you to come to the meeting early. What verb means 'to politely request'?
a1-n-briefmarke: You put a small colourful picture in the corner of the envelope so that the post office will deliver your letter.
A boy collects small pictures from letters of many countries in an album.
At the post office you ask for a small paper to stick on your postcard to Spain. What is it called?
a1-n-heimat: After ten years abroad, the old man dreams of the place where he was born and grew up.
The refugee says he misses the country and town where he comes from and where his family lives.
A song talks about a feeling of belonging to the place you come from. Which noun means this place?
a1-adv-zirka: You say that the trip takes not exactly, but roughly two hours. Which adverb means 'roughly'?
The seller says there are not exactly, but around fifty people at the party. Which word, short for 'around' or 'about', is used?
The teacher says the book has about 200 pages. Which adverb means 'approximately'?
a1-n-mittwoch: The day in the middle of the working week, between Tuesday and Thursday.
You have a doctor's appointment in the middle of the week at 4 p.m. Which day?
A shop is closed on Wednesday afternoons. Which day of the week is that?
a1-v-studieren: After school, you go to university and choose medicine as your subject for the next six years.
Your sister is enrolled at the university and attends lectures in biology.
A friend asks what you are doing after school. You say you will attend university for a degree.
a1-pr-anderer: You do not like this jacket, so you ask the seller to show you a different one.
The teacher says that some pupils are finished, but the rest of the pupils are not. Which word means 'the rest, different from these'?
The first bus is full, so you wait for a different one. Which word means 'different' or 'another one'?
a1-n-schluessel: When you come home, you take a small metal object from your pocket and push it in the lock to open the door.
You lose the thing you need for your car. Without it you cannot start the engine.
The hotel gives you a plastic card with the number 214 for your room, in place of a metal one.
a1-adj-kurz: The skirt only reaches to the top of the knee. It is not long.
The film is only twenty minutes long, which is not long at all.
A friend says that the trip to the shop took only a few minutes. Which adjective is the opposite of 'long'?
a1-n-wein: At the dinner with your fish, you drink a glass of red or white drink from grapes.
In the south of Germany, near the river, there are many farms with vines that make this drink.
At the restaurant the waiter suggests a bottle of red to go with your steak. What does he bring?
a1-n-schueler: A boy of twelve carries a heavy school bag and goes to class every day.
The teacher says that one of the boys in her class has not done his homework.
At the bus stop in the morning there are many boys and girls going to school. A male one is called what?
a1-v-ausziehen: You come home, are tired, and take off your coat, shoes and trousers before bed.
The doctor says: please take off your shirt, so that I can listen to your heart.
Your sister has found a flat and is leaving her parents' house to live on her own.
a1-n-haehnchen: At the grill stand you buy a half bird with golden skin and potatoes.
The recipe says: put the farm bird in the oven for an hour with spices and lemon.
Many fast food restaurants serve fried pieces of this bird with chips. Which meat is it?
a1-n-wasser: After the run you are thirsty and take a bottle of clear liquid with no taste.
You turn on the tap in the kitchen and a clear liquid runs out. You use it to wash and drink.
The doctor says that you should drink two litres a day of the liquid that is neither juice nor wine.
a1-v-ueberweisen: You pay your rent by sending money from your bank account to your landlord's account.
The doctor cannot treat your knee, so he sends you to a special doctor, an orthopaedist.
You use your banking app to send fifty euros to your brother's account.
a1-n-gast: A man arrives at your party. You invite him in, and offer him food and a drink, because he is not a member of your family.
In a hotel, a person who pays for a room and stays for the night is called what?
At the restaurant the waiter says to the manager that a person at table five wants to pay.
a1-adv-viel: You work long hours and have a large amount of work. You say you work a great deal. Which adverb means 'a lot'?
A friend asks if you like football. You say: yes, very much. Which adverb means 'much'?
Your friend says the new flat is way bigger than the old one. Which adverb goes before 'bigger' for emphasis?
a1-adj-richtig: The teacher says that your answer in the test is exactly what she wanted, without mistake.
At the quiz show, the host says: your answer is right. Which adjective means 'not wrong'?
You are on the correct road to the station. A passer-by confirms: yes, this is the right way. Which adjective?
a1-n-wohnung: You rent three rooms with a kitchen and a bathroom in a building with many floors.
On the internet you look at ads for a place to live in the city centre, with two bedrooms and a balcony.
When you move out of your parents' house, you look for a place of your own with a kitchen and bathroom. What do you look for?
a1-n-internet: At the cafe, you ask for the password for the wireless connection, so that you can search websites and read emails.
At home your computer shows no connection, so you cannot read the news or watch videos online.
A grandfather asks what the network is that connects computers all over the world. Which noun?
a1-v-wiederholen: The teacher says that you should say the sentence a second time, because the pronunciation was not clear.
Your friend did not understand you on the phone, so you say it again, slowly.
Before the exam, you read through the old vocabulary again and again, to remember it.
